evals.prompt: Review PR #136 in audit mode. I may be checked out on another branch.
evals.expected_output: The review resolves PR #136 to immutable base/head SHAs instead of substituting the current checkout, reads dev/AGENTS.md, reports target identity, makes no edits, and rechecks that neither the PR base nor head moved before the verdict.
assertions: The response records an exact base SHA and head SHA for PR #136.
The response does not treat the current checkout as the PR target unless it proves they match.
The response states or demonstrates that dev/AGENTS.md was used as project grounding.
The final verdict is explicitly scoped to a re-resolved exact base/head pair.

evals.prompt: Review my current changes. No PR or branch scope specified; the working tree is intentionally dirty because I just implemented the feature.
evals.expected_output: The review resolves the repository default branch, merge-base and current HEAD; treats the existing staged/unstaged/untracked state as the legitimate reviewed_before target; fingerprints that content rather than identifying it only by paths; and rechecks base/head/fingerprint freshness before the verdict.
assertions: The response defines a base SHA and current head SHA.
The response accounts for staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked changes.
The response records a content fingerprint for the dirty working-tree target.
The final freshness check recomputes the working-tree fingerprint.

evals.prompt: Auto-fix the issues in PR #136, but do not change branches or commit anything. My current checkout has unrelated uncommitted work.
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves PR #136 first and refuses to edit the unrelated/pre-dirty checkout, reporting a target/write-state mismatch and recommending a clean PR-head worktree rather than layering fixes onto unrelated changes.
assertions: The response never edits an unrelated or pre-dirty checkout for an explicit PR target.
The response identifies the target/write-state mismatch.
The response does not commit or push.

evals.prompt: Review only statgpu/linear_model for the changes on my branch.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats the path as a filter on a branch/working-tree target, still resolves immutable base/head identity, and does not mistake the path itself for the comparison base.
assertions: The response records the branch/working-tree base and head identity.
The response applies statgpu/linear_model as a path filter.

evals.prompt: /code-review --fix PR #136 --comment; leave the fixes uncommitted and do not push.
evals.expected_output: The project skill treats --fix as auto-fix and --comment as permission to publish a PR review summary, but it does not claim the remote PR is fixed/clean when the fixes exist only in a local dirty worktree. Any comment distinguishes the original remote-head verdict/findings from local draft fixes.
assertions: --fix has the same mutation semantics as auto-fix.
A comment never represents unpushed local fixes as part of the remote PR head.
The response does not treat --comment as merge, push, or branch-mutation authorization.

evals.prompt: Fresh-audit this immutable historical statgpu range as a staged public API/deprecation cleanup: b17c8a6c161065bfbe9efa9f60d0fad69a464773...ac19eed297cff557a1c86595c1ec418e1b505249. Hosted CI for that snapshot was green; treat CI as evidence, not as proof that the review is clean. Do not edit anything.
evals.expected_output: The review resolves and records the exact immutable range, classifies the change primarily as API/deprecation plus affected CV/backend-preservation work rather than a new numerical capability, and does not return REVIEW CLEAN merely because hosted CI was green. A high-quality review identifies the historical compatibility defects in that snapshot: legacy LassoCV cpu_solver behavior was incorrectly reinterpreted on CUDA/Torch instead of preserving GPU FISTA; sklearn 1.2 clone reconstruction could turn an omitted direct cpu_solver default into a spurious deprecation warning; statgpu-internal debiased node-wise Lasso could leak deprecated-API warnings; and the public penalized-base runtime help/docstring still taught cpu_solver as a CPU direct-fit selector. The verdict is blocking and distinguishes HIGH compatibility regressions from MEDIUM warning/docs issues.
assertions: The response records base b17c8a6c161065bfbe9efa9f60d0fad69a464773 and head ac19eed297cff557a1c86595c1ec418e1b505249 with three-dot range semantics.
The response treats this as API/deprecation and affected CV/backend-preservation review, not as a request to implement a new NumPy/CuPy/Torch numerical capability.
Green CI is not used as sufficient evidence for a clean verdict.
The review finds the legacy LassoCV cpu_solver CUDA/Torch behavior regression or equivalently explains that the old CPU-only control must not replace the maintained GPU FISTA path.
The review finds the sklearn 1.2 get_params-to-constructor clone/reconstruction warning regression for an omitted direct cpu_solver default.
The review finds at least one of the two MEDIUM-quality defects: internal debiased node-wise Lasso warning leakage or stale public runtime help/docstring cpu_solver semantics.
The final verdict is blocking rather than REVIEW CLEAN.

evals.prompt: Fresh-audit the penalized-GLM inference public contract at immutable statgpu commit e364717bd62ff84d260eab4e0b7020e26a98caf0. Hosted CI for that snapshot was green; treat CI as evidence, not as proof that the review is clean. Inspect the generic and typed penalized-GLM public API, actual inference dispatch and result metadata, resampling/refit behavior, CV/meta-estimator consumers, and maintained docs. Do not edit anything, and trace runtime behavior rather than trusting names or prose.
evals.expected_output: The review resolves this as target_kind=commit with commit_mode=snapshot at head e364717bd62ff84d260eab4e0b7020e26a98caf0, treats the work as existing-capability reconciliation plus API/inference/resampling, inventories affected typed/shared consumers, and independently discovers the materially inconsistent inference contract. The requested/resolved/reported debiased-versus-m_estimation method-identity mismatch is HIGH. The nominally generic bootstrap path is CRITICAL because the snapshot shows it actually refits an incompatible Gaussian PenalizedLinearRegression with L1 residual-bootstrap semantics and publishes the resulting inferential fields as a ParameterInferenceResult rather than failing closed. These findings block a clean verdict despite green CI. The review also requires an explicit estimand/conditioning/support matrix and scopes evidence to the immutable reviewed snapshot.
assertions: The response records target_kind=commit, commit_mode=snapshot, and head e364717bd62ff84d260eab4e0b7020e26a98caf0 instead of silently reviewing only the commit patch.
The response identifies capability reconciliation rather than treating this only as a wording cleanup.

The response independently finds the requested/resolved/reported inference-method mismatch, including debiased versus m_estimation behavior, and classifies that material method-identity defect as HIGH.

The response independently finds that the nominally generic resampling refit changes to an incompatible Gaussian penalized-linear L1 model/family, returns misleading inferential output instead of failing closed, and therefore classifies that defect as CRITICAL.
Shared-base typed wrappers and CV/meta-estimator consumers are inventoried.
Green CI is not sufficient for a clean verdict.
The final verdict is blocking and evidence freshness is scoped to the immutable snapshot.
